source_snapshot.test_name_items: Set LAN source in DHCP via BIOS
source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Set LAN source by:
    - Boot into setup menu and move to the BMC networking page.
    - Set the source to "via DHCP" then save and exit.
2. Boot into OS
3. Send command: ipmitool lan print to check LAN information.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: BMC LAN should get an IP address from DHCP server.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- not runnable by agent: this path sets the LAN source to DHCP through the BIOS setup menu (boot into setup -> BMC networking page -> set source -> save & exit). Navigating BIOS setup menus and saving is interactive Pre-OS work the agent cannot drive over SSH/ipmitool; the result must be seen in BIOS.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: operator boots into BIOS setup, sets BMC network source to 'via DHCP' on the BMC networking page, saves & exits, then boots to OS; agent could afterwards only confirm via `ipmitool lan print` that the channel obtained a DHCP address.

historical_reviews.deepseek: NO correctly protects the BIOS interaction boundary and mentions post-boot `lan print`, but misses that the source-defined readback, DHCP lease correlation and recovery are meaningful automatable portions and supplies no network-loss safeguards.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: MANUAL ONLY / CHANGED provides strong BIOS/menu, DHCP/MAC, alternate recovery and rollback controls but classifies the whole hybrid case as manual despite the explicit post-boot electronic verification.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 816/2291 treats the case as purely physical and asks only for operator evidence, overlooking the source-required `ipmitool lan print` and authoritative DHCP-server evidence.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Its non-counting sequence-981 draft was inspected only as history. This review independently reclassifies the case as package/user confirmation under the policy rule for BIOS/manual action plus automatable post-check, while preserving the BIOS control path as irreplaceable coverage.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-33 preserves the explicitly required BIOS method and records any Project override as different coverage; ED-36 treats menu/channel/DHCP inputs as readiness; ED-38 keeps BIOS save, reboot, network loss and verdict engineer-owned.

original_test_intent: Verify the platform BIOS BMC-network integration by selecting DHCP in the actual pre-OS setup page, saving the configuration, booting the OS, then proving the mapped BMC interface obtained the intended DHCP lease and remains recoverably manageable. The BIOS path itself—not merely the final DHCP state—is part of coverage.
original_method: A qualified operator enters the version-specific BIOS setup, navigates to the BMC network page, changes the source to `via DHCP`, saves/exits and boots the OS. Automation then reads the mapped BMC LAN state and correlates it with the DHCP server lease and BMC identity; it must not perform an IPMI/WebUI configuration write as a substitute.
manual_activity: A qualified operator confirms the target and maintenance window, navigates the BIOS menu, captures the original/selected value, saves/exits, supervises the reboot and maintains local/serial recovery while the BMC address changes. Automation performs only the approved post-boot readback and lease/identity correlation.
required_inputs: Exact platform/BIOS/BMC revisions and authoritative setup path, writable versus read-only behavior, save/activation semantics and approved final value
Mapping from the BIOS BMC network selection to physical port, shared/dedicated interface, IPMI channel, BMC MAC/VLAN and current management path
DHCP server/scope/VLAN, reservation or policy, client identifier, expected subnet/gateway, acquisition timeout and server lease-log access
Full prior BMC network configuration, quiescent host/reboot approval, local console plus independent BMC rediscovery/recovery and tested BIOS/network rollback
Protected post-boot BMC access, ipmitool/approved readback version, operator evidence capture and synchronized boot/network timeline
safety_requirements: Do not replace BIOS navigation/save with `ipmitool lan set`, WebUI or another API; those can reach DHCP without testing the source's BIOS integration path.
Before saving, verify the BIOS menu is for the intended BMC interface and preserve the original setting and full network configuration; do not guess from a similar platform menu.

A save may restart/readdress the BMC and the host reboot interrupts service. Confirm a dedicated/quiescent SUT, immutable chassis identity, local console and an independent recovery observer that does not rely on the changing BMC IP.
Use an isolated approved DHCP/VLAN environment and correlate the lease to the recorded BMC MAC/client ID; do not accept the first responsive address or stale lease.
Do not automate unverified BIOS keystrokes, expose credentials, clear logs, retry a failed save/boot or repeatedly toggle the setting.

Abort on unexpected BIOS option, wrong interface/MAC, DHCP address outside policy, no lease within timeout, boot failure/loop, loss of all recovery paths or inability to restore the original configuration.
After evidence collection, restore the approved final BIOS/network mode if required, save/reboot once under approval and verify host, BMC identity, management reachability and settings readback.
agent_execution_scope: Before execution, validate the BIOS/menu/interface/DHCP/reboot/recovery package without changing DUT state.
After the operator's approved BIOS save and reboot, collect protected read-only mapped-channel LAN data, DHCP-server lease evidence, BMC identity, host boot markers and management reachability.
Correlate the BIOS selection/save evidence with the resulting DHCP lease; report any post-boot IPMI/WebUI write as a prohibited coverage substitution rather than recovery success.
Do not enter BIOS, send keystrokes, save settings, reboot, configure BMC networking, expose credentials, auto-retry or issue DUT PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve the BIOS path/setting, interface map, DHCP plan, maintenance window, reboot, recovery, rollback and final state.
Perform and document the BIOS selection/save and reboot while maintaining console/alternate recovery and confirming physical/BMC identity.
Restore and verify the approved configuration after evidence capture and issue the verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Correctly rejects remote substitution for BIOS navigation. Its proposed later `lan print` is a valid source-required post-check, but only on the mapped channel and recovered BMC and only when correlated with the intended DHCP server lease.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Keep BIOS setting/save manual. After the operator completes it, use protected read-only `ipmitool lan print <approved-channel>` or the platform-supported equivalent plus DHCP server logs and immutable BMC identity; no configuration command is recommended.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: BIOS setup BMC-network page, `via DHCP`, save/exit, OS boot, `lan print`, no Script and 10/10-minute estimates remain unmodified.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Snapshot configuration and identity; record the exact BIOS DHCP selection and save; observe reboot/BMC readdressing from independent paths; correlate server lease to MAC; verify mapped-channel source/address and management usability after OS boot; then restore/verify the approved final state.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact BIOS-BMC network integration, chassis port topology, VLAN and DHCP infrastructure.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BIOS, BMC, NIC/CPLD, SDR, ipmitool and DHCP server versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform BIOS BMC-network menu specification, channel/port mapping, DHCP policy and Project recovery approval.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds deterministic identity, lease proof, reboot/readdress observation and rollback without replacing the required BIOS interaction.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A post-boot DHCP state set through IPMI/WebUI provides no evidence that BIOS displayed, saved, propagated or persisted the setting; readback alone is supporting evidence.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Menu/setting, interface map, DHCP identity, reboot, recovery and final-state approval.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: The combined BIOS save, host reboot and BMC readdress can simultaneously remove both host and management access if recovery is not independent.

project_override_considerations: A Project may approve a different menu path or automation-capable pre-OS console, but must still exercise the BIOS-owned setting and document equivalence. A BMC-side IPMI/WebUI override is different-path coverage and cannot claim this BIOS testcase PASS.
expected_evidence: Platform/BIOS/BMC identity, authoritative menu path, interface/channel/port/MAC map, DHCP policy and full pre-change BIOS/network state
Operator/console evidence of original value, selecting `via DHCP`, save/exit result and single approved boot timeline
DHCP discovery/request/ack or authoritative lease record correlated to the recorded BMC MAC/client ID and approved scope/timing
Post-boot full mapped-channel readback showing DHCP source/address/subnet/gateway/MAC, same-BMC identity and management reachability
Approved final setting restoration/readback, host/BMC recovery, unexpected log review, no substitute configuration writes and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure and Criteria align on BIOS-configured DHCP followed by post-boot verification. Platform-specific menu, interface and lease values are readiness inputs, not contradictory semantics.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The BIOS target, operation and DHCP result are understandable. With the platform package and operator approval, the manual setup plus automated post-check is executable; missing inputs do not create a permanent block.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Preserves its manual BIOS boundary but recognizes the source-required electronic post-check and adds identity-safe DHCP/recovery evidence.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains its strong safety analysis but changes MANUAL ONLY to package/user confirmation because the case has a material automatable post-boot verification phase.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces physical-only evidence with the complete BIOS-save-to-lease-to-readback chain.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Agrees that the BIOS path cannot be replaced, while correcting its manual-only class under the current hybrid-case rule.

review_improvement: Prevents both common false positives: crediting an IPMI-side DHCP change to the BIOS path, and accepting a post-boot address without proving it was issued to the same BMC by the intended DHCP environment.
independent_technical_reasoning: The function under test is pre-OS BIOS propagation into BMC networking, so manual navigation/save is indispensable. The Master also defines a programmatic LAN readback, and reliable acceptance requires server-side lease correlation and recovery. That meaningful split makes the case hybrid and therefore package/user confirmation rather than manual-only or blocked.
